symptom: A suite with one test that does not build (CE0161 in an XPath that passes `mxcli check`) ended `mxcli test --local` in "Passed: 0, Errors: 1, Skipped: 108", and read as if every test had failed for no reason. Separately, a `mxbuild --serve` that stopped answering ended the run in "local runtime: build: serve build request to http://127.0.0.1:6544/build: ... context deadline exceeded", and the next run passed with nothing changed
cause: The build error was attributed (since mendixlabs/mxcli#1104) but printed only on its ERROR row, among one SKIP row per other test that each repeated "not run: another test in this run failed to build" — the cause was present and buried. The boot's build called `ServeServer.Build` once, so a wedged serve process was reported as the run's error although a fresh process builds the same project fine
insight: Surfacing is about position, not presence: the error had been in the output for months. Put it directly above the summary line, where the eye lands at the end of a long run. For the retry, retry only on a timeout (`net.Error.Timeout()`), once, on a FRESH process — a failed build is the model's verdict and a refused connection is a dead process, and retrying either hides it. The fake timeout in the unit test is cross-checked against a real `http.Client{Timeout}` error wrapped as `ServeServer.Build` wraps it, so the detection cannot pass against a shape net/http never produces. Runtime control on 11.12.2 with a real CE0161 test: main printed the error on its row only, the fix also in the block above the summary
